races.name: Faucets The Bathroom Specialists Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB Race)
Birthday Boy Leighton Happy 80th Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: The Coffee Pod
runners_data.note: A hold-up operator for Muir & Grassick who needs others to cut it up in front; only 8 days since last run and 0 wins from 15 similar-going runs makes this a tough ask at OR 62, though the fresh return is noted.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, The Coffee Pod brings solid fitness — just eight days between runs — and experience over today's trip and conditions. Third last time out suggests he retains ability, and our rating of 75 marks him as the one to beat from stall eight.

runners_data.name: Miracleoftheandes
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Warren Greatrex with solid recent form (2nd on Good over 5f); 18 days since last run is fine, and this horse must be respected as the pace anchor who could dictate if Sheik Yerbouti cries enough early.
runners_data.comment: Miracleoftheandes shaped with plenty of promise when second two starts back, and she has run over today's trip, arrives here in fine fettle just 18 days since her last outing, and a rating of 65 marks her as a live threat from stall 3; the concern is she remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Portacloy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Kubler yard who switches to 5f after a run of 6f form; trainer at 7/16 in the 14-day window signals in-form stable, and the drop in trip and switch to Good turf suits his profile as a horse who wants to be involved throughout.
runners_data.comment: Portacloy won five starts back but has since finished unplaced and then eighth, sixth, and fifth in her last four, suggesting she's struggling to recapture that form; distance and going experience help, and 21 days between runs leaves her reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Dark Sun
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has won over 5f on Good ground and shows a 1W3P record from 15 similar-going starts; Laura Coughlan's 3lb claim is a practical bonus, and this horse is the standout closer in the field if the pace truly collapses.
runners_data.comment: Dark Sun shaped well when third last time out and is a winner three starts back, bringing proven fitness on 18 days' rest, experience over today's trip and going, and a respectable rating in fourth place on our figures; the risk is that she has to overcome stall nine carrying 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Sheik Yerbouti
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a fade-in-finish flag who has been off 57 days; the layoff is a genuine concern at 5f where you need to be sharp from the gate, and if he fades early he simply hands the initiative to Miracleoftheandes rather than creating the pace war this shape assumes.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Sheik Yerbouti faces a stiff ask here; he was third last time out, though an absence of 57 days and a hefty 134 lb to carry add further doubt, despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Little Jaybee
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for David Evans who carries a fade flag and has finished 8th or 9th in three of his last five starts; J F Egan's booking is the best thing about this runner, but a record of 0W1P from 10 similar-going efforts is uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Little Jaybee nonetheless shaped with clear promise when third last time out, and she has run over today's distance and going before; the worry is whether she can convert that form into a telling challenge from stall four off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Happier
runners_data.note: Trainer Keighley has this horse down to a career-low OR of 55, and the horse has won over 5f on Standard; however, this is a genuine hold-up type mapped into midfield on the pace chart because the field has a surplus of backmarkers, meaning it is unlikely to race in its natural position and the STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 reflects a material discount to its chance.
runners_data.comment: Happier won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid platform, but she carries 130 lb from stall 5 and her earlier form in recent starts has been patchy — she'll need to reproduce that latest effort to figure here.

runners_data.name: River Edge
runners_data.note: OR 45 but boasts a strong 5f Good-ground profile with consistent placing form (2nd, 3rd, 4th, 4th, 4th from six similar-going efforts); also a natural hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map due to the clustering of rear-runners — the redistribution tempers expectation, but course-trip-going alignment is the most compelling in this group.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, River Edge does at least return 19 days fresh with experience of today's distance and going — though a sequence of two fourth-place finishes and an official rating of just 45 make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Miss Gold
runners_data.note: A filly stepping sharply back from 6f-8f to 5f carrying a fade flag and an 0W0P record from four similar-going runs; the redistribution into midfield compounds an already awkward profile, and the step down in trip looks speculative rather than planned.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a string of ninth-place finishes and an unplaced effort that make her hard to fancy here — our figures rank her last of nine in this field. Has run over today's trip and going before, which is at least something.

races.paceDynamic: Miracleoftheandes and Sheik Yerbouti are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this sharp 5f at Ffos Las, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft-pedal opening. On Good turf with no pace concession, the two leaders are likely to push each other through the first two furlongs at an honest clip, which sets up a race that plays into the hands of horses who can sit just off the speed and pounce when the front two come back to them inside the final furlong. Sheik Yerbouti carries a fade flag and a 57-day absence, so Miracleoftheandes may assert for control, but the pace effect remains the same — a contested lead burning energy early. This shape most directly suits prominent-to-midfield types who travel smoothly in the slipstream rather than true closers, and the runners tagged as redistributed (Happier, River Edge, Miss Gold) are genuine hold-up horses pushed into the midfield bracket on the map because the field holds more hold-up types than the pace shape can naturally accommodate at the rear; of those three, River Edge has the most relevant form profile for this track and trip and is most likely to extract value from whatever gaps appear, though none of the three will get an ideal position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Miracleoftheandes and Sheik Yerbouti burn each other up at the front, a prominent racer sitting a length or two off the pace collects.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other through the first half of the race, and the horse who has tracked them without exerting herself swoops in the final 100 yards as the leaders empty.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Asserts Fully
scenarios.trigger: If Miracleoftheandes shakes off Sheik Yerbouti early and dictates a controlled gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: With Sheik Yerbouti failing to sustain a challenge — as his fade flag and lay-off suggest is possible — Miracleoftheandes gets a soft lead and simply gallops rivals into the ground on this flat, unforgiving 5f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace is fierce enough to detonate both front-runners before the final furlong, leaving a gap for the backmarkers.
scenarios.body: Dark Sun, who has won over this course and distance on Good ground, is the best-credentialed closer in the field and would be the primary beneficiary, looming late as the pace implodes.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race fractures chaotically and genuine closers thread through from the rear in the dying strides.
scenarios.body: This shape depends on Happier, River Edge, or Miss Gold racing in their true hold-up role, but all three are redistributed in the pace map and unlikely to get that clean position; the scenario is discounted accordingly, with River Edge's strong Good-ground 5f course record the only credible hook.

watchPoints.text: Sheik Yerbouti's 57-day absence combined with his fade-in-finish flag means watch him in the opening furlong — if he is slow away or immediately outpaced by Miracleoftheandes, the assumed pace contest collapses into a unilateral lead scenario.
Portacloy needs to secure his prominent position from stall draw before the pace heats up; if he gets crowded or shuffled back in the first two furlongs, he loses the race shape that suits him most.

Dark Sun's hold-up style is the most reliable closer in the race, but on a flat 5f at Ffos Las there is limited room to make up ground — watch whether the early pace is truly honest enough to bring the rear runners into play at all.

River Edge has the best course-trip-going alignment of the hold-up group, but as a redistributed runner forced out of its natural rearward position, watch whether Gina Mangan can find a tactical slot mid-race or whether the horse simply gets shuffled into an uncomfortable no-man's-land.

The cluster of three redistributed hold-up types (Happier, River Edge, Miss Gold) all seeking a similar position means there may be interference or checking in midfield as the pace develops — watch the first two furlongs for positional scrimmaging between this group.

races.name: Meyer Timber EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Dandara Homes Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Nammos
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has won twice over 8f on Firm and shaped well on Good, but his OR=55 mark and trainer T14 strike rate of 1/8 temper enthusiasm; Carson rides and the uncontested lead is the key asset, though his similar-going record reads only 5/15 0W0P suggesting the form on this surface is limited.
runners_data.comment: Nammos shaped well when second three starts back and has experience of today's trip and going to call upon, but she'll need to reverse two subsequent fifth-place finishes to make her presence felt from stall 10 carrying 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Angel's Call
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good and placed over the same trip, giving her the most relevant course-and-distance profile in the field; natural hold-up style suits a race where the pace may compress the field, and the tongue-tie (hg:p) is noted, though Kavanagh's 3lb claim is a small help on the handicap.
runners_data.comment: Angel's Call won last time out but that sole success in his last six starts tells its own story, and our figures rank him eighth of ten here. The 43-day break adds a fitness query, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Kev
runners_data.note: Returns after 85 days off for Muir & Grassick, who have a busy yard (T14:3/24) but this horse's recent form figures of 0,9,8 on Good and Standard are deeply uninspiring, and the finishing fade flag compounds concern — the layoff and form trajectory both point away from involvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 85 days off, Kev faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's trip before and a rating of 53 offers marginal encouragement from stall six at 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Rival
runners_data.note: Stablemate of Nammos under Flint and partnered by the experienced Muscutt; has placed three times over 8f on Good ground and finished second over this course and trip, giving him a legitimate claims as the horse most likely to benefit from sitting just off the leader's shoulder in the tactical scenario this race sets up.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Rival nonetheless brings solid experience of today's trip and conditions, and 28 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the main concern is that his recent finishing positions have been trending in the wrong direction.

runners_data.name: Oviedo
runners_data.note: Consistent run of finishes in 9th or 10th suggests this mare finds little once off the bridle; a true hold-up horse whose redistribution to midfield on the map reflects the crowded rear-guard — she has never won in 15 similar-going starts and the STYLE_FIT flag underlines the structural disadvantage she faces here.
runners_data.comment: Oviedo has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him clear of his rivals, but his recent form — winless in his last five starts, including three ninths — offers little encouragement from stall five off 75 days.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Four places from eight starts on Good going is the most encouraging line in his record, and he showed 3rd over 8f here on this surface; though he's a hold-up type squeezed forward on the map, he has enough positional flexibility to get closer than some of the other redistributed runners — Murphy's 7lb claim is a bonus.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in his last six starts — third last time out and a second three starts back — King Of The Dance has run over today's trip and going and returns fit on a quick 15-day turnaround; the risk is he remains winless and that mid-race exit leaves a blot on the form.

runners_data.name: Uncle Albert
runners_data.note: Wintle has a strong T14 strike rate (4/17) but this gelding has not finished above 6th in any of his last five starts, all on softer surfaces, and the finishing fade flag is a significant warning; a genuine hold-up horse shifted toward midfield on the map, he is unlikely to reach a competitive position on this flat track.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and a modest official mark of 45 underline the task facing Uncle Albert, though our rating suggests a shade more ability than that; he has run over today's trip and going before, and 50 days off may have freshened him up.

runners_data.name: Change Of Fortune
runners_data.note: Steps back from 10-12f trips to a mile, which is a concern given his last five runs have all been at longer distances on softer ground; a natural closer whose sole similar-going start produced a 1/15 record, and the drop in trip on Good turf looks a significant ask despite Jack Callan's booking.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and 58 days off the track, Change Of Fortune does at least have experience of today's trip and going, and a draw of two to note; third two starts back shows ability, but that ninth last time out is the concerning angle.

runners_data.name: Ivat Ghia
runners_data.note: The youngest runner in the field at three, Heard takes the ride on this hold-up type who placed second over 8f on Good — the most recent of his four career starts; the tongue-tie (hg:h) is noted, the sim-going record of 2/4 with one place is modest but more relevant than several rivals', and he is honest if limited.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a pair of sixths and an eighth punctuating a recent second, Ivat Ghia is hard to fancy off a rating of 52 — yet that runner-up finish shows she has competed respectably, and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Big Moonrise
runners_data.note: Returning from 197 days off (LR:197d) for David Evans, who has placed one from 14 recently; a three-year-old with just three career starts all at 7f on Standard — stepping up to a mile on Good turf with no relevant form, and a STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90 after redistribution makes this a significant ask on comeback.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and absent for 197 days, Big Moonrise faces a stiff task here; a third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement, and he has run over today's trip before, but returning from such a lengthy break makes him hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Nammos is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of ten, and with no confirmed pace rival to press him, he is likely to coast along at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over the Ffos Las mile. The bulk of the field — Oviedo, King Of The Dance, Big Moonrise, Uncle Albert, and Change Of Fortune — are genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers to place at the back, meaning several of them will be forced to race closer to the pace than they would naturally choose. With Nammos uncontested and likely to control a steady tempo, the race shape strongly favours a horse who can race prominently or in a tracking position just behind the leader — setting up a stamina-based grind to the line that punishes those forced wide late from deep in the pack. The tactical verdict is clear: prominent racers who can travel close to Nammos and pounce turning in hold the structural advantage; deep closers face a more difficult task against a pace that is unlikely to be truly searching.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nammos Controls, Rival Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Nammos sets a steady, uncontested lead and the pace remains moderate throughout the mile.
scenarios.body: Nammos dictates every yard from the front at a sustainable gallop, and Rival, tracking prominently in second or third, has the perfect position to deliver a measured challenge in the final two furlongs. This shape suits horses close enough to the pace to benefit from a leader who sets an honest but not punishing tempo, with the winner emerging from the front two-thirds of the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace compresses the field and a genuine hold-up specialist finds a gap late.
scenarios.body: Angel's Call, who won over this course and distance on Good ground, would be the chief beneficiary if a bunched mid-race procession creates enough daylight in the straight for a late charge. Ivat Ghia, who placed second over 8f on Good, also profiles as a horse that could close from the rear if the finishing straight opens up sufficiently.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Nammos Outstayed
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to secure a closer position and the pace picks up sharply in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: King Of The Dance, who has placed four times in similar company and holds course form, would be best placed among the redistributed runners to exploit a mid-race acceleration given his consistent proximity to the pace in recent runs. However, the STYLE_FIT discounts on several in this scenario lower its overall likelihood, as many of these horses are not naturally suited to securing the tracking role this shape demands.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Pace Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If Nammos sets an unusually slow tempo and the race degenerates into a sprint for home with little early gallop.
scenarios.body: In this scenario, the finishing speed of a lightly-raced type like Big Moonrise or Ivat Ghia could surprise the field if class handicappers are caught flat-footed in the scrimmage to the line. However, Big Moonrise is returning from 197 days off and has not won, making this the least probable outcome in a race where Nammos is expected to at least ensure a controlled pace.

watchPoints.text: Rival is positioned to be the chief beneficiary of Nammos's uncontested lead — watch whether Muscutt slots him directly into second or third at the break, as that position is the pivot point for the most likely race shape.

King Of The Dance (hg:p, tongue-tie) has the best similar-going placing record among the redistributed hold-up types — if Murphy manages to secure a tracking berth rather than being forced wide late, he could outrun his redistribution discount.

The field contains at least five genuine hold-up horses all attempting to find positions near the rear — watch the first two furlongs to see if there is any traffic bunching or shuffling for position that could compromise several runners' races simultaneously.

Big Moonrise returns from 197 days off with no form over a mile or on Good going — monitor his pre-race market moves as any significant support from the David Evans yard would be the only meaningful reason to take him seriously on this occasion.

Angel's Call won over this course and trip on Good — if the pace is slow enough to bring hold-up horses into the finish, she has the most relevant course-and-distance credentials of any closer in the race and warrants monitoring in the betting.

races.name: Golwg Gwendraeth "Confined" Handicap Stakes (For Horses Which Have Not Won A Flat Race In 2026)

runners_data.name: Port Louis
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has hit the frame at 1m on Good ground but carries a habit of fading late in the finish; Bernard Llewellyn's operation has limited recent firepower at 1/4 in 14 days, and Charlie Tucker's 7lb claim softens the weight burden — but this horse's natural hold-up style means it needs more pace than The Stone Power is likely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Port Louis was third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, so conditions pose no concern; yet to score in his last six, he remains a lively contender from stall one carrying 135 lb fresh enough on 20 days' rest.

runners_data.name: Next Guilian
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's three-year-old showed fair form on Good ground at 8f across two of his last three starts and returns after a 30-day break at the top of the weights for its age; Darragh Keenan is a capable jockey and the Good going suits, making this one of the better-placed horses given its ability to race prominently if needed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with finishes of fifth, sixth, eighth, and third four starts back, Next Guilian rates below the field on our figures; experience over today's trip and going and a 30-day break offer slim encouragement, but he faces a stiff task from stall five off a mark of 70.

runners_data.name: The Stone Power
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and holds the key tactical advantage in this race; Rhys Clutterbuck can dictate at a comfortable clip, and the style-fit flag (0.93) only reflects the mapping displacement rather than undermining what is a genuine positional edge — Beckett's yard is active at 4/39 in the past 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in recent starts and clearly capable on his day, The Stone Power has run over today's trip and is rated our second best of these carrying 134 lb from stall four on a quick 12-day turnaround — the pulled-up effort last time is the one thing punters must forgive.

runners_data.name: Royal Bodyguard
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old has placed on Good ground multiple times at distances up to 10f and Daniel Muscutt — a high-calibre jockey — brings significant steering value for a horse that must hold a tracking position just off The Stone Power; 54 days since last run is the one flag, though the Going suits and the form profile over 8f is the strongest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and fourth last time out, Royal Bodyguard has run over today's trip and going, rates highest of the six on our figures, and carries a workable 132 lb from stall two — though a 54-day absence and a trainer firing at just 5% are the risks.

runners_data.name: John Harrison
runners_data.note: Alan King's three-year-old finished third twice and placed at 8f and 10f on Good ground, and Luke Catton's 3lb claim helps at the weights — but this horse's instinctive preference for being held up late means it is mapped to midfield against its will, and the likely absence of a searching gallop diminishes its chance materially.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, John Harrison brings solid each-way claims having finished third last time out and third two starts back, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour from stall three. The main risk is that he remains winless in his last five outings.

runners_data.name: Brave New World
runners_data.note: Ed Walker — whose barn is firing at 9/43 over the last 14 days — sends this lightly-raced three-year-old for just its fourth career start, stepping up from 7f; the horse has finished seventh on all three runs to date including on Good ground, and while the step up in trip could theoretically suit, it arrives as the lowest-rated runner in the field and carries the most doubt.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts — including back-to-back seventh-place finishes — Brave New World has experience over today's trip but shaped poorly throughout, and at 49 on our figures he ranks last of six, making him very difficult to fancy here.

races.paceDynamic: The Stone Power is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of six and faces no meaningful pace pressure, giving Rhys Clutterbuck a free rein to dictate terms at whatever tempo suits his mount on Good ground over one mile at Ffos Las. With Port Louis, John Harrison, and Brave New World all genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the pace map — simply because the field cannot accommodate that many closers at the rear — the true shape of this race is a single horse controlling affairs with a loose-leader advantage throughout. That uncontested lead on a flat track and honest Good ground strongly favours those who can sit close enough to The Stone Power to avoid conceding too much early ground; pure closers will need a searching gallop that is unlikely to materialise. This race shape decisively favours prominent and close-tracking runners who can hold a position just behind the leader and pounce in the straight, rather than true hold-up horses whose finishing kicks depend on a contested early pace that simply will not be supplied.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stone Power Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If The Stone Power goes unchallenged in front and sets a moderate, sustainable gallop that saps the finishing kick of hold-up types.
scenarios.body: The Stone Power bowls along uncontested, conserving energy into the home straight, and the proximity riders who track him within two lengths are ideally placed to challenge; pure closers find themselves with too much ground to make up against a horse that has never been stretched.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Tracker Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sitting second or third tracks The Stone Power to the turn and outstays him in the final furlong on Good ground.
scenarios.body: Royal Bodyguard or Next Guilian, positioned just off the pace, benefits as The Stone Power ties up inside the final furlong; Good ground form for both makes this credible, and Daniel Muscutt's positional awareness suits the stalking role.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Get Lucky Break
scenarios.trigger: If The Stone Power sets a surprisingly strong early pace that brings hold-up runners into play at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Port Louis or John Harrison, despite being mapped out of their natural rearward position, benefit if an unexpected injection of tempo opens the race up; both carry history of finishing into the frame on Good ground, though their redistribution means this requires an atypical scenario to unfold.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset From the Handicap Basement
scenarios.trigger: If Brave New World, freshened after 41 days off and aided by Ashley Lewis's claim, improves sharply on its flat debut form.
scenarios.body: Ed Walker's operation has strong recent strike rate at 9/43 over the 14-day window, and stepping up from 7f to a mile could unlock hidden stamina in a lightly-raced three-year-old; however, three consecutive finishing positions of 7th and a lack of Good-ground experience make this the longest of the plausible outcomes.

watchPoints.text: Watch The Stone Power's early stride pattern — if Rhys Clutterbuck eases out from the gate and is immediately unchallenged, the race is effectively controlled from the front and all challengers must account for the free lead.

Royal Bodyguard's 54-day absence is the primary fitness query; if Daniel Muscutt is instructed to ride conservatively on a horse that needs race-fitness, it may be too far back to reel in The Stone Power in a slow-run mile.

Port Louis has a documented tendency to fade in the closing stages and is being ridden by a 7lb claimer — if it attempts to sit closer than its natural style dictates, an early fade in the straight is a realistic outcome that could compromise other runners' paths.

John Harrison and Brave New World are both running out of their natural positional roles; if either rider tries to force a prominent early position, it could create a brief injection of pace in the first two furlongs that would reshape the race for late finishers.

Brave New World's step up from 7f to 1m on Good turf for Ed Walker is worth monitoring in the market — any significant support for a horse with three seventh-place finishes would suggest connections have seen improvement at home ahead of this entry.

races.name: Dress For The Occasions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Meet Me In Meraki
runners_data.note: David Evans gelding who has placed three times on Good ground in similar company; hold-up by nature but capable of travelling closer in a small field, and six furlongs shorter than his last two runs suggests this 1m4f trip is squarely in his wheelhouse — John Egan is the key booking here.
runners_data.comment: Improving of late with a third two runs back and a runner-up finish last time out, Meet Me In Meraki has experience over today's trip and going and arrives here fresh on 29 days' rest — yet to score in his last six, that winless run is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Bulldog Spirit
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn's six-year-old has placed on Good ground at 1m4f-1m6f and carries the tongue-piece today; at 29 days since his last run he arrives fresh, and Daniel Muscutt can be expected to place him just off the pace in a race that suits his staying profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bulldog Spirit nonetheless rates narrowly top of these on our figures and has experience of today's distance and going; third last time out, 29 days fresh, and carrying 142 lb, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Noble Grace
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's five-year-old won over 1m4f on Good ground most recently and is his trainer's most active runner this fortnight (2/6 T14); in truth a genuine hold-up horse that will be operating further back than the map's midfield slot implies, so a strong pace is needed to bring his late kick into play.
runners_data.comment: Noble Grace arrives on the back of a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and going, making her a lively danger here; the main concern is whether she can defy a burden of 140 lb against stronger opposition.

runners_data.name: Belle Of Kt
runners_data.note: J S Moore's mare arrives on a two-race winning run, both coming over 1m4f-1m6f, and is the only horse in this field likely to lead — Millie Wonnacott (5) will be given a clear brief to dictate, and on Good ground her style fit at this course and distance is high despite the STYLE_FIT flag relating to map position.
runners_data.comment: Belle Of Kt ranks last on our figures and her official mark of 54 leaves her with plenty to find, though she arrives fit on a 12-day turnaround and her recent back-to-back wins give her genuine each-way claims if that form translates.

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: David Flood's lightly-weighted three-year-old has won three times on Good ground and is the freshest runner in the field at just 8 days since last racing; a genuine hold-up type shunted into a midfield slot on the map, she will likely race further back still, needing this to be run at a genuine clip to land her late effort.
runners_data.comment: A Daughters Love won last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, with a lively recent record of three wins in her last six starts; the main risk is whether she can back it up off just eight days.

runners_data.name: Claytons Kolatonic
runners_data.note: Dominic Ffrench Davis's three-year-old is making a dramatic step up in trip from 8f to 1m4f having shown zero form beyond a distant place in five turf starts; 58 days off the track and entirely unexposed at this distance, he is a true hold-up runner whose chance depends on how quickly he adapts to the longer test.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a ninth last time out and a seventh two starts back, Claytons Kolatonic heads here after 58 days off carrying 129 lb — a stiff ask for a horse rated 59 on his official mark, and he looks hard to fancy at the foot of the rankings.

races.paceDynamic: Belle Of Kt is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no genuine rival to press her from the gates, she will control the tempo entirely from her own counsel on Good ground at Ffos Las. The pace she sets is likely to be honest but comfortable — a mare who has won twice recently and clearly relishes dictating — making this a race run to suit those who can race close to the tempo rather than those forced to make up ground from the rear. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the back: Noble Grace, A Daughters Love, and Claytons Kolatonic are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots on the map, meaning at least some of them will find themselves racing even further back than their natural position suggests. This shape — a single uncontested leader controlling a moderate gallop on flat, Good turf over 1m4f — strongly favours horses able to race prominently or in close order behind the pace, as the finish is likely to be decided by those who have tracked Belle Of Kt and can sustain into the straight without needing to manufacture momentum from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Belle Controls, Close Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Of Kt bowls along uncontested and the few horses able to sit close behind her (Meet Me In Meraki, Bulldog Spirit) track within striking range throughout.
scenarios.body: Belle Of Kt sets a manageable pace, the closers just off her shoulder travel smoothly and have enough in reserve to challenge over the final two furlongs; the winner is almost certainly among those who raced in the first three or four throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Swooper Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to crack the leader and one of the true hold-up horses (Noble Grace, A Daughters Love) manages to thread through late.
scenarios.body: A sustained gallop stretches the field and creates a proper end-to-end race, giving a horse with a late kick a clear run up the straight; Noble Grace, a proven winner on Good ground over this trip, is best positioned of the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Belle Of Kt Leads And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace Belle sets proves just slow enough that she conserves energy and the pursuing pack is unable to muster a serious challenge entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Belle Of Kt's recent winning form at 1m2f-1m4f and her willingness to make her own running suggests she can get away from the field if allowed to dictate entirely unchallenged; Millie Wonnacott (5) riding a confident front-running race would be the key execution.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Late
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Of Kt is ridden too aggressively early and fades sharply inside the final two furlongs, leaving the race wide open for whichever hold-up horse has settled best.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability scenario given Belle's recent strong form and her handler's evident front-running intent; Claytons Kolatonic, stepping up sharply in trip from 8f on Good ground, is the wild card if others fail to sustain.

watchPoints.text: Belle Of Kt is allowed a completely uncontested lead — if Wonnacott is given a hands-and-heels ride in front, the margin she builds by the home straight could prove decisive and should not be underestimated.

Noble Grace, A Daughters Love, and Claytons Kolatonic are all genuine hold-up horses packed into the rear half; watch for traffic complications in the straight if all three are angling for the same gap behind Belle Of Kt.

A Daughters Love is only 8 days since her last run and has shown a habit of making errors when asked to win — if Darragh Keenan cannot get a clear passage from the back, her late run may arrive too late on a flat, straightforward track.

Claytons Kolatonic steps from 8f to 1m4f with 58 days off — monitor his early behaviour in the market; any significant drifting in price would suggest connections themselves are uncertain about the trip and fitness combination.

Bulldog Spirit's trainer Bernard Llewellyn has just one winner from four runners in the last 14 days — note whether Muscutt is instructed to ride him closer than usual, as a revised tactical approach in a small field could alter this horse's place prospects markedly.
